s0001.literal: Second year, spring, first month, on bingzi day, an edict remitted corvée purchase and market purchase for relay households of the two capitals.
s0001.idiomatic: Second year, spring, first month, on bingzi day, an edict remitted corvée purchase and market purchase for relay households of the two capitals.

s0002.literal: On jimao day, an edict ordered that Jiangnan must not capture swans.
s0002.idiomatic: On jimao day, an edict ordered that Jiangnan must not capture swans.

s0003.literal: Because garrison-farming laborers under Hulachu's ten-thousand-household office were impoverished, the rent they owed was remitted.
s0003.idiomatic: Because garrison-farming laborers under Hulachu's ten-thousand-household office were impoverished, the rent they owed was remitted.

s0004.literal: Huang Shengxu, rebel bandit of Shangsi Prefecture, attacked and plundered the Siguang stockade at Shuikou; the Huguang branch secretariat mobilized troops, broke them, and captured his followers Huang Fa'an and others; the bandits fled into Shangya Liuluo.
s0004.idiomatic: Huang Shengxu, rebel bandit of Shangsi Prefecture, attacked and plundered the Siguang stockade at Shuikou; the Huguang branch secretariat mobilized troops, broke them, and captured his followers Huang Fa'an and others; the bandits fled into Shangya Liuluo.

s0005.literal: On renwu day the moon encroached upon Yuhui.
s0005.idiomatic: On renwu day the moon encroached upon Yuhui.

s0006.literal: An edict ordered that for all households subordinate to keshik, no one was to contend over them.
s0006.idiomatic: An edict ordered that for all households subordinate to keshik, no one was to contend over them.

s0007.literal: On jiashen day Prince of Xiping Aoluchi was ordered to reside at Shangdu this summer.
s0007.idiomatic: On jiashen day Prince of Xiping Aoluchi was ordered to reside at Shangdu this summer.

s0008.literal: On bingxu day Venus appeared in daylight.
s0008.idiomatic: On bingxu day Venus appeared in daylight.

s0009.literal: Prince Anxi's tutor Tiechi, Tuotuomu'er, and others again requested establishment of a princely chancellor's office; the Emperor said: "Last year Ananda already stated this in person; We instructed him with Shizu's established regulations; now you again memorialize — do you wish to make all of Sichuan and Jingzhao entirely yours?
s0009.idiomatic: Prince Anxi's tutor Tiechi, Tuotuomu'er, and others again requested establishment of a princely chancellor's office; the Emperor said, "Last year Ananda already stated this in person; We instructed him with Shizu's established regulations; now you again memorialize — do you wish to make all of Sichuan and Jingzhao entirely yours?

s0010.literal: Tax levies and military relay stations are all under court administration; for now We shall accede to your request and establish a princely chancellor's office, but it may handle only princely-tutor affairs."
s0010.idiomatic: Tax levies and military relay stations are all under court administration; for now We shall accede to your request and establish a princely chancellor's office, but it may handle only princely-tutor affairs."

s0011.literal: On dinghai day the moon encroached upon Pingdao.
s0011.idiomatic: On dinghai day the moon encroached upon Pingdao.

s0012.literal: On jichou day censorate officials said: "Han Chinese who serve as colleagues have often had their crimes gathered up by wicked men, and therefore dare not speak fully.
s0012.idiomatic: On jichou day censorate officials said, "Han Chinese who serve as colleagues have often had their crimes gathered up by wicked men, and therefore dare not speak fully.

s0013.literal: We request selecting men from among close attendants Sibaozhi and Sugurji."
s0013.idiomatic: We request selecting men from among close attendants Sibaozhi and Sugurji."

s0014.literal: The Emperor said: "What use are such men?
s0014.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What use are such men?

s0015.literal: Select Han Chinese who understand affairs and are competent to serve."
s0015.idiomatic: Select Han Chinese who understand affairs and are competent to serve."

s0017.literal: On gengyin day the moon encroached upon Gouqin.
s0017.idiomatic: On gengyin day the moon encroached upon Gouqin.

s0018.literal: On xinmao day Ochicharu, Bolad, and guards under Helazhi's command were ordered to transport army grain themselves; their travel expenses were supplied.
s0018.idiomatic: On xinmao day Ochicharu, Bolad, and guards under Helazhi's command were ordered to transport army grain themselves; their travel expenses were supplied.

s0019.literal: On jiawu day Zhang Yucai, thirty-eighth-generation successor Han Celestial Master, was granted the title Perfect Man of Supreme Purity, Numinous Concentration, and Expansive Way and put in charge of Daoism on all Jiangnan circuits.
s0019.idiomatic: On jiawu day Zhang Yucai, thirty-eighth-generation successor Han Celestial Master, was granted the title Perfect Man of Supreme Purity, Numinous Concentration, and Expansive Way and put in charge of Daoism on all Jiangnan circuits.

s0020.literal: On yiwei day, an edict ordered that princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law must not punish officials without receiving an imperial order; Prince Heban's consort was granted one thousand two hundred ingots of notes and one thousand bolts of miscellaneous silks and cloths; imperial son-in-law Tahai Temür was granted three thousand ingots of notes.
s0020.idiomatic: On yiwei day, an edict ordered that princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law must not punish officials without receiving an imperial order; Prince Heban's consort was granted 1,200 ingots of notes and 1,000 bolts of miscellaneous silks and cloths; imperial son-in-law Tahai Temür was granted 3,000 ingots of notes.

s0021.literal: Uighur Bolad Khan presented lions, leopards, and medicinal substances; he was granted more than one thousand three hundred ingots of notes.
s0021.idiomatic: Uighur Bolad Khan presented lions, leopards, and medicinal substances; he was granted more than 1,300 ingots of notes.

s0022.literal: Second month, yihai new moon: central secretariat officials said: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, what has been granted to princes, princesses, imperial sons-in-law, and meritorious ministers has been no small amount; what was formerly stored has nearly all been dispersed.
s0022.idiomatic: Second month, yihai new moon: central secretariat officials said, "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, what has been granted to princes, princesses, imperial sons-in-law, and meritorious ministers has been no small amount; what was formerly stored has nearly all been dispersed.

s0023.literal: Those who continue to request are still many; we beg to grant only to the destitute and those going to the frontier; the rest should all be stopped."
s0023.idiomatic: Those who continue to request are still many; we beg to grant only to the destitute and those going to the frontier; the rest should all be stopped."

s0025.literal: Ten thousand troops from the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat were divided to garrison Huguang.
s0025.idiomatic: 10,000 troops from the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat were divided to garrison Huguang.

s0026.literal: Chenghai garrison-farming troops were supplied with agricultural implements.
s0026.idiomatic: Chenghai garrison-farming troops were supplied with agricultural implements.

s0027.literal: An edict ordered that where envoys or military officers died and their sons had not yet inherited office, the gold and silver tallies they wore were to be returned to the government; violators were punished.
s0027.idiomatic: An edict ordered that where envoys or military officers died and their sons had not yet inherited office, the gold and silver tallies they wore were to be returned to the government; violators were punished.

s0028.literal: On xinchou day the Central Imperial Guard Office was established; Tughbuqa and Tangwu were both made directors of the central guard.
s0028.idiomatic: On xinchou day the Central Imperial Guard Office was established; Tughbuqa and Tangwu were both made directors of the central guard.

s0029.literal: On bingwu day military commanders were forbidden privately to swap guard troops and Mongol troops; those who used household slaves to substitute for service were punished, and the slaves were separately entered into military registers and half their master's assets given them; commanders who dared condone it were dismissed.
s0029.idiomatic: On bingwu day military commanders were forbidden privately to swap guard troops and Mongol troops; those who used household slaves to substitute for service were punished, and the slaves were separately entered into military registers and half their master's assets given them; commanders who dared condone it were dismissed.

s0030.literal: Reaching adult age among Mongol households was registered to fill the ranks.
s0030.idiomatic: Reaching adult age among Mongol households was registered to fill the ranks.

s0031.literal: On dingwei day the moon encroached upon Jing.
s0031.idiomatic: On dingwei day the moon encroached upon Jing.

s0032.literal: On gengxu day, an edict ordered that soldiers who privately exchanged assignments or fled and returned were put to death.
s0032.idiomatic: On gengxu day, an edict ordered that soldiers who privately exchanged assignments or fled and returned were put to death.

s0033.literal: Tutuhe's division was supplied with garrison-farm agricultural implements.
s0033.idiomatic: Tutuhe's division was supplied with garrison-farm agricultural implements.

s0034.literal: On bingchen day, an edict ordered that Jiangnan Daoist priests who traded or held land must pay land and commercial taxes.
s0034.idiomatic: On bingchen day, an edict ordered that Jiangnan Daoist priests who traded or held land must pay land and commercial taxes.

s0035.literal: On gengshen day households under Jarligh Qutuqhu's command residing at Fengsheng and Yunzhou were to share corvée equally with commoners.
s0035.idiomatic: On gengshen day households under Jarligh Qutuqhu's command residing at Fengsheng and Yunzhou were to share corvée equally with commoners.

s0036.literal: From Liupan Mountain to the Yellow River garrison-farm fields were established; ten thousand troops were stationed.
s0036.idiomatic: From Liupan Mountain to the Yellow River garrison-farm fields were established; 10,000 troops were stationed.

s0037.literal: On bingyin day Duan Zhen, Dadu intendant, was made vice grand councillor of the central secretariat.
s0037.idiomatic: On bingyin day Duan Zhen, Dadu intendant, was made vice grand councillor of the central secretariat.

s0038.literal: Envoys were dispatched to perform sacrificial substitutes at the peaks and rivers.
s0038.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to perform sacrificial substitutes at the peaks and rivers.

s0039.literal: Three thousand shi of rice was granted to Prince Anxi to relieve famine victims.
s0039.idiomatic: 3,000 shi of rice was granted to Prince Anxi to relieve famine victims.

s0040.literal: Third month, on renshen day Buhua, vice grand councillor of the central secretariat, was made Hanlin academician-expositor of the Zhaowen Hall and vice councillor for military and state affairs.
s0040.idiomatic: Third month, on renshen day Buhua, vice grand councillor of the central secretariat, was made Hanlin academician-expositor of the Zhaowen Hall and vice councillor for military and state affairs.

s0041.literal: Brewing and presenting grape wine at Taiyuan and Pingyang routes was abolished; commoners who relied on grape gardens as their livelihood were all restored to them.
s0041.idiomatic: Brewing and presenting grape wine at Taiyuan and Pingyang routes was abolished; commoners who relied on grape gardens as their livelihood were all restored to them.

s0042.literal: More than three thousand weak tammaq troops under Prince Chuban's command requested replacement with strong men; approved; also ordered that Chuban must not privately mobilize troops without an imperial order.
s0042.idiomatic: More than 3,000 weak tammaq troops under Prince Chuban's command requested replacement with strong men; approved; also ordered that Chuban must not privately mobilize troops without an imperial order.

s0043.literal: Because people at Qerlur summer residence suffered famine, each household was given six months' grain.
s0043.idiomatic: Because people at Qerlur summer residence suffered famine, each household was given six months' grain.

s0044.literal: Prince Qingtong was ill; his son Yelibuhua was made to replace him.
s0044.idiomatic: Prince Qingtong was ill; his son Yelibuhua was made to replace him.

s0045.literal: Princes Basar, Huo'erhudasun, and Tula were each granted one thousand ingots of notes.
s0045.idiomatic: Princes Basar, Huo'erhudasun, and Tula were each granted 1,000 ingots of notes.

s0046.literal: Investigating censor Wanseng accepted bribes; the censorate and Xuanzheng Bureau commissioner Dashman were jointly ordered to try the case.
s0046.idiomatic: Investigating censor Wanseng accepted bribes; the censorate and Xuanzheng Bureau commissioner Dashman were jointly ordered to try the case.

s0047.literal: On guiyou day summer-stationed troops were increased to forty thousand men.
s0047.idiomatic: On guiyou day summer-stationed troops were increased to 40,000 men.

s0048.literal: Xindu said Prince of Jin Gammala and Do'erdai said Yue'erlu each harbored secret designs; an edict ordered the privy council to interrogate them; nothing was verified.
s0048.idiomatic: Xindu said Prince of Jin Gammala and Do'erdai said Yue'erlu each harbored secret designs; an edict ordered the privy council to interrogate them; nothing was verified.

s0049.literal: The Emperor ordered death for the one who accused the Prince of Jin, and the one who accused Yue'erlu was banished to military service to redeem himself.
s0049.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered death for the one who accused the Prince of Jin, and the one who accused Yue'erlu was banished to military service to redeem himself.

s0050.literal: An edict ordered the Yunnan regional censorate to examine and impeach the case documents of the Yiqibusi pacification commission.
s0050.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Yunnan regional censorate to examine and impeach the case documents of the Yiqibusi pacification commission.

s0051.literal: On jiaxu day Princes Yisizhili, Babusha, Yilinzhen, Yeliqian, and Wengjiladai were all dispatched to summer-station at Prince of Jin Qerlur's territory.
s0051.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Princes Yisizhili, Babusha, Yilinzhen, Yeliqian, and Wengjiladai were all dispatched to summer-station at Prince of Jin Qerlur's territory.

s0052.literal: On bingzi day the imperial carriage visited Shangdu.
s0052.idiomatic: On bingzi day the imperial carriage visited Shangdu.

s0053.literal: On dingchou day Wanyan Bangyi, Nasuding, and Liu Ji'an were sentenced for presumptuously discussing court affairs: beaten, sentenced to two years' exile, and half their household property confiscated.
s0053.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wanyan Bangyi, Nasuding, and Liu Ji'an were sentenced for presumptuously discussing court affairs: beaten, sentenced to two years' exile, and half their household property confiscated.

s0054.literal: On jiashen day the Emperor halted at Dakou.
s0054.idiomatic: On jiashen day the Emperor halted at Dakou.

s0055.literal: On yiyou day the moon encroached upon Gouqin.
s0055.idiomatic: On yiyou day the moon encroached upon Gouqin.

s0056.literal: On xinmao day thirty thousand shi of grain was granted to the Liaoyang branch secretariat.
s0056.idiomatic: On xinmao day 30,000 shi of grain was granted to the Liaoyang branch secretariat.

s0057.literal: On renchen day, an edict ordered Imperial Son-in-law Yidu Hu to register dispersed Uighur households.
s0057.idiomatic: On renchen day, an edict ordered Imperial Son-in-law Yidu Hu to register dispersed Uighur households.

s0058.literal: On guisi day the Huguang branch secretariat sent to the capital Lu Wanchou and Wang Xian, followers of the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu.
s0058.idiomatic: On guisi day the Huguang branch secretariat sent to the capital Lu Wanchou and Wang Xian, followers of the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu.

s0059.literal: Prince Temür was granted two hundred fifty taels of gold, two thousand five hundred taels of silver, and five thousand ingots of notes to honor his battle merit.
s0059.idiomatic: Prince Temür was granted 250 taels of gold, 2,500 taels of silver, and 5,000 ingots of notes to honor his battle merit.

s0060.literal: Because the people under Hebo and Tatara suffered famine, one thousand shi of relief rice was granted to each.
s0060.idiomatic: Because the people under Hebo and Tatara suffered famine, 1,000 shi of relief rice was granted to each.

s0061.literal: Summer, fourth month, jihai new moon: Sadishmiss was ordered to gather the dispersed people under his ancestor Mangudai's command.
s0061.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, jihai new moon: Sadishmiss was ordered to gather the dispersed people under his ancestor Mangudai's command.

s0062.literal: Prince Babusha was granted forty thousand ingots of notes; Yezhen's division sixty thousand ingots.
s0062.idiomatic: Prince Babusha was granted 40,000 ingots of notes; Yezhen's division 60,000 ingots.

s0063.literal: Jiangzhou of Pingyang, Huangyan Prefecture of Taizhou Route suffered famine; Hangzhou suffered fire; all were given relief.
s0063.idiomatic: Jiangzhou of Pingyang, Huangyan Prefecture of Taizhou Route suffered famine; Hangzhou suffered fire; all were given relief.

s0064.literal: Fifth month, wuchen new moon: corvée of the two capitals was remitted.
s0064.idiomatic: Fifth month, wuchen new moon: corvée of the two capitals was remitted.

s0065.literal: On xinwei day Prince Anxi sent envoys reporting destitution; the Emperor told them: "Shizu, because of the difficulty of divided grants, once gave a sacred instruction, which Ananda also knows.
s0065.idiomatic: On xinwei day Prince Anxi sent envoys reporting destitution; the Emperor told them, "Shizu, because of the difficulty of divided grants, once gave a sacred instruction, which Ananda also knows.

s0066.literal: If you speak of destitution, are you alone in that?
s0066.idiomatic: If you speak of destitution, are you alone in that?

s0067.literal: Last year twenty thousand ingots of notes were granted, and grain was also supplied; if We grant now, the princes will think it uneven;
s0067.idiomatic: Last year 20,000 ingots of notes were granted, and grain was also supplied; if We grant now, the princes will think it uneven;

s0068.literal: If We do not grant, you say many people are starving to death.
s0068.idiomatic: If We do not grant, you say many people are starving to death.

s0069.literal: Grant ten thousand shi of grain and distribute it to relieve the destitute."
s0069.idiomatic: Grant 10,000 shi of grain and distribute it to relieve the destitute."

s0070.literal: On jiaxu day, an edict ordered: among private horses, cattle, and sheep of the people, one in a hundred was taken; where sheep numbered fewer than a hundred they were still taken; only semuren and nursing lambs were exempt.
s0070.idiomatic: On jiaxu day, an edict ordered: among private horses, cattle, and sheep of the people, one in a hundred was taken; where sheep numbered fewer than a hundred they were still taken; only semuren and nursing lambs were exempt.

s0071.literal: On dingchou day the moon encroached upon Pingdao.
s0071.idiomatic: On dingchou day the moon encroached upon Pingdao.

s0072.literal: On gengchen day Tubo rebelled, killing and plundering troops and civilians of Jie Prefecture; Toghto was dispatched to join Prince Temür Budaq, Jilie, and others in combined forces to suppress them.
s0072.idiomatic: On gengchen day Tubo rebelled, killing and plundering troops and civilians of Jie Prefecture; Toghto was dispatched to join Prince Temür Budaq, Jilie, and others in combined forces to suppress them.

s0073.literal: On jiashen day Yezhen and Seshan were ordered to summer-station at Heyier territory.
s0073.idiomatic: On jiashen day Yezhen and Seshan were ordered to summer-station at Heyier territory.

s0074.literal: Princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law were forbidden to recruit households.
s0074.idiomatic: Princes, princesses, and imperial sons-in-law were forbidden to recruit households.

s0075.literal: On jichou day, an edict ordered that all those sentenced to penal corvée be released within one year and not flogged.
s0075.idiomatic: On jichou day, an edict ordered that all those sentenced to penal corvée be released within one year and not flogged.

s0076.literal: On gengyin day tribute of single-stalk scallions from Mahu in Sichuan was abolished.
s0076.idiomatic: On gengyin day tribute of single-stalk scallions from Mahu in Sichuan was abolished.

s0077.literal: An edict ordered households of princes, imperial sons-in-law, and meritorious ministers with allotted domains.
s0077.idiomatic: An edict ordered households of princes, imperial sons-in-law, and meritorious ministers with allotted domains.

s0078.literal: Those residing at Shangdu, Dadu, and Longxing were to share provision and corvée equally with commoners.
s0078.idiomatic: Those residing at Shangdu, Dadu, and Longxing were to share provision and corvée equally with commoners.

s0079.literal: On dingyou day branch secretariats were ordered not to mobilize troops without receiving an imperial order.
s0079.idiomatic: On dingyou day branch secretariats were ordered not to mobilize troops without receiving an imperial order.

s0080.literal: The kingdom of Annam sent men to entice the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu.
s0080.idiomatic: The kingdom of Annam sent men to entice the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu.

s0081.literal: Yeheimi presented red sandalwood; he was granted four thousand ingots of notes.
s0081.idiomatic: Yeheimi presented red sandalwood; he was granted 4,000 ingots of notes.

s0082.literal: That month, wild silkworms formed cocoons.
s0082.idiomatic: That month, wild silkworms formed cocoons.

s0083.literal: Yishi County in Hezhong Prefecture suffered hail;
s0083.idiomatic: Yishi County in Hezhong Prefecture suffered hail;

s0084.literal: Pingjin in Taiyuan, Jiaohe and Leshou in Xian Prefecture, Mo Pavilion and Renqiu in Mo Prefecture, and Liling Prefecture in Hunan all suffered flooding;
s0084.idiomatic: Pingjin in Taiyuan, Jiaohe and Leshou in Xian Prefecture, Mo Pavilion and Renqiu in Mo Prefecture, and Liling Prefecture in Hunan all suffered flooding;

s0086.literal: Sixth month, on jihai day seven thousand two hundred-odd horses were granted to Prince Chuban's troops.
s0086.idiomatic: Sixth month, on jihai day 7,200-odd horses were granted to Prince Chuban's troops.

s0087.literal: An edict ordered that clothing and grain for the Prince of Jin's following: grain was granted annually, clothing every three years.
s0087.idiomatic: An edict ordered that clothing and grain for the Prince of Jin's following: grain was granted annually, clothing every three years.

s0088.literal: Relay households at Guazhou and Shazhou were supplied with oxen and farm implements.
s0088.idiomatic: Relay households at Guazhou and Shazhou were supplied with oxen and farm implements.

s0089.literal: Censorate officials said: "Where officials accepted bribes, at first they confessed, but upon subsequent review officials who showed favor caused them to change their testimony; we request increased punishment by one grade."
s0089.idiomatic: Censorate officials said, "Where officials accepted bribes, at first they confessed, but upon subsequent review officials who showed favor caused them to change their testimony; we request increased punishment by one grade."

s0091.literal: On yisi day Venus encroached upon Tianguan.
s0091.idiomatic: On yisi day Venus encroached upon Tianguan.

s0092.literal: Because mobilizing troops had harmed farming, field rent in Rong Prefecture and other places in Guangxi was remitted for one year.
s0092.idiomatic: Because mobilizing troops had harmed farming, field rent in Rong Prefecture and other places in Guangxi was remitted for one year.

s0093.literal: On bingwu day the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu fled into Jiaozhi.
s0093.idiomatic: On bingwu day the rebel bandit Huang Shengxu fled into Jiaozhi.

s0094.literal: On jiayin day regulations on bribery by officials were promulgated, thirteen grades in all.
s0094.idiomatic: On jiayin day regulations on bribery by officials were promulgated, 13 grades in all.

s0095.literal: On dingsi day Venus encroached upon Saturn.
s0095.idiomatic: On dingsi day Venus encroached upon Saturn.

s0096.literal: On guihai day the moon encroached upon Jing.
s0096.idiomatic: On guihai day the moon encroached upon Jing.

s0097.literal: On bingyin day, an edict ordered branch secretariats and regional censorates not to stop whatever Zhu Qing submitted.
s0097.idiomatic: On bingyin day, an edict ordered branch secretariats and regional censorates not to stop whatever Zhu Qing submitted.

s0098.literal: Prince of Xiping Aoluchi was granted two hundred fifty taels of silver and six thousand ingots of notes; his following sixty thousand ingots; Prince Yilinzhen's following two hundred thousand ingots; Ulus winter-stationed troops thirty thousand ingots.
s0098.idiomatic: Prince of Xiping Aoluchi was granted 250 taels of silver and 6,000 ingots of notes; his following 60,000 ingots; Prince Yilinzhen's following 200,000 ingots; Ulus winter-stationed troops 30,000 ingots.

s0099.literal: That month, locusts in Dadu, Baoding, Bianliang, Jiangling, Mianyang, Huai'an, Taiping, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Shaoxing, Jiankang, Lizhou, Yuezhou, Luzhou, Runing, Longyang Prefecture, Hanyang, Jining, Dongping, Daming, Huazhou, and Dezhou; hail in Datong, Longxing, Shunde, and Taiyuan.
s0099.idiomatic: That month, locusts in Dadu, Baoding, Bianliang, Jiangling, Mianyang, Huai'an, Taiping, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Shaoxing, Jiankang, Lizhou, Yuezhou, Luzhou, Runing, Longyang Prefecture, Hanyang, Jining, Dongping, Daming, Huazhou, and Dezhou; hail in Datong, Longxing, Shunde, and Taiyuan.

s0100.literal: The people of Hainan suffered famine; grain was issued to relieve them.
s0100.idiomatic: The people of Hainan suffered famine; grain was issued to relieve them.
